nodes.name: AAO templated NiFe electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: A thin Au layer of thickness of about 70 nm was first deposited on one side of the AAO membrane by using an SPI carbon and sputter systems. A copper foil was then placed on the conductive side (Au layer side) of the AAO membrane for electrodeposition. The copper foil was used as a conductive support to facilitate the electrodeposition of NiFe alloy and was removed after the electrodeposition. The electrolyte for the electrodeposition contained mixed precursors of nickel sulfate hexahydrate (NiSO4·6H2O) and ferrous sulfate heptahydrate (FeSO4·7H2O) at a total molar concentration of 1 M at increasing Fe concentrations of 100:0, 97.5:2.5, 95:5, 90:10, and 85:15 for Ni:Fe. The electrolyte also contained boric acid of 40 g L⁻¹ and saccharin of 1 g L⁻¹. The electrodeposition was conducted in a three-electrode system with a power supply of a CHI6275D electrochemical workstation. The working electrode (AAO) and counter electrode (Pt foil of 1×1 cm²) was separated by 1.5 cm and Ag/AgCl served as the reference electrode. The electrodeposition proceeded for 5400 s at a constant voltage of -2 V (vs EAg/AgCl).
nodes.source_text: Fabrication of NiFe Nanowire Arrays: A thin Au layer... The electrodeposition proceeded for 5400 s at a constant voltage of -2 V (vs EAg/AgCl).

nodes.name: AAO template removal
nodes.procedure: The electrodeposited AAO was then washed with deionized (DI) water and subjected to etching in 0.5 M NaOH solution for 60 min, followed by sonication for 5 min to remove the AAO layer. Finally, the NiFe nanowire array or Ni nanowire array was cut into pieces of 0.5 cm × 1 cm in size, soldered, and sealed with epoxy resin to obtain the electrode for electrochemical characterizations.

nodes.name: NiFe nanowire sulfurization
nodes.procedure: The NiFe nanowire array was immersed in 0.05 M Na2S solution at 90 °C for 12 h. The sample was then collected and rinsed with DI water several times to remove possible residuals.
nodes.source_text: Sulfurization of NiFe Nanowire Arrays: The NiFe nanowire array was immersed in 0.05 M Na2S solution at 90 °C for 12 h.

nodes.source_text: The best performing OER electrode, S-NiFe10 NWA, and HER electrode, NiFe0 NWA, were coupled for overall water splitting, with S-NiFe10 NWA serving as the anode and NiFe0 NWA serving as the cathode.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe10 nanowire array shows nanowires of length around 36 μm and diameter around 260 nm matching AAO pore size of 250 nm. S-NiFe10 develops interwoven nanosheet structure on surfaces.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the pore size of the AAO membrane is around 250 nm, from which NiFe NWAs with nanowires of length around 36 μm (Figure 2b) and diameter around 260 nm (Figure 2c) are obtained... morphology of the NiFe nanowires after surface sulfurization was observed with SEM... interwoven nanosheet structure appears on the surfaces of the NiFe nanowires.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe NWAs show Ni (FCC) phase with peaks at 44.1° (111), 51.3° (200), 75.6° (220); grain sizes decrease from 14.6 nm (pure Ni) to 6.5 nm (NiFe15). S-NiFe10 retains NiFe peaks plus minor (Ni,Fe)3S2 peaks at 21.8°, 31.2°, 37.9°, 50.2°, 55° slightly shifted right due to Fe incorporation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The three main diffraction peaks located at the 2θ values of 44.1°, 51.3°, and 75.6° can be indexed to the (111), (200), and (220) crystalline planes... grain size... decreases with increasing Fe loading, 14.6, 14.3, 7.9, 7.3, and 6.5 nm... five minor diffraction peaks located at 21.8°, 31.2°, 37.9°, 50.2°, and 55°... slightly shifted to the right.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe10 NWA: 45 mol% Fe, confirms EDX composition. S-NiFe10: S 2p at 163.5 eV (2p1/2), 162.3 eV (2p3/2); Ni 2p shifts from 873.8/855.9 eV to 872.8/855.0 eV; Fe 2p from 725.8/712.2 eV to 724.6/711.4 eV confirming M-S formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: 43 versus 45% determined for Fe by EDX and XPS... S 2p1/2 and S 2p3/2 at 163.5 and 162.3 eV... Ni 2p1/2, Ni 2p3/2, Fe 2p1/2, and Fe 2p3/2 at 873.8, 855.9, 725.8, and 712.2 eV... shift to 872.8, 855.0, 724.6, and 711.4 eV.

nodes.characterization_summary: S-NiFe10 nanowires show core/shell structure with NiFe core and (Ni,Fe)3S2 shell. Interlayer distances of 0.404 nm (101) and 0.285 nm (110) for sulfide shell, 0.205 nm (111) for NiFe core.
nodes.evidence_snippet: two distinct domains can be identified, the inner one for NiFe and the outer one for (NiFe)3S2... Interlayer distances of 0.404 and 0.285 nm are determined, corresponding to the (101) and (110) crystalline planes.

nodes.characterization_summary: S-NiFe10 NWA shows characteristic Ni3S2 peaks at 239, 302, 326, and 350 cm⁻¹ confirming sulfide formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: four characteristic Raman peaks located at 239, 302, 326, and 350 cm⁻¹ are identified for the S-NiFe10 NWA, corresponding well to those of Ni3S2.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe NWAs show Fe content much higher than electrolyte due to anomalous deposition; NiFe15 is Fe-rich (60%). Uniform Ni/Fe/S distribution confirms uniform sulfide shell on S-NiFe10.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the molar ratios of Fe in the product nanowires are much higher than the molar ratios of Fe in the corresponding electrolytes. For the case of 15% Fe precursor, the NiFe alloy becomes Fe-rich (60%)... uniform elemental distributions of Ni, Fe, and S on the nanowire.
